$comment: PT-7501 OLTC and HV bushing twin. Expected values in Maximo Monitor from nameplate, OLTC, regulator and bushing data; the device sends only what it measures.

twin.name: Power transformer PT-7501: on-load tap-changer and HV bushings

identification.manufacturer: Grid transformer with Maschinenfabrik Reinhausen OLTC and OIP HV bushings
identification.model: 60 MVA 132/33 kV, OLTC VACUTAP VRS III 700 Y, motor drive ETOS, bushings OIP type GOB class
identification.description: Grid transformer T1 of a 132/33 kV primary substation: on-load tap-changer and HV bushing twin
identification.transformer: 60 MVA ONAF, 132/33 kV, YNd11, HV tapping +/-10 % in 16 steps at the HV neutral end (assumption: typical design)
identification.oltc: Maschinenfabrik Reinhausen VACUTAP VRS III 700 Y (vacuum diverter switch, change-over selector), 17 positions
identification.motor_drive: MR ETOS motor-drive unit; TAPCON voltage regulator (automatic voltage control)
identification.bushings: 3 x HV condenser bushings, oil-impregnated paper (OIP), porcelain, 2 kV test tap (for example Hitachi Energy GOB class)
identification.monitoring: Bushing monitor on the test taps (for example MR MSENSE BM-T: C1 and tan delta per bushing), OLTC monitoring in the motor drive, OLTC oil temperature and online DGA in the OLTC and main tank oil

transformer.source: Rated power, voltages, vector group, short-circuit impedance uk and load losses: assumption: typical value, replace with your nameplate and routine test report (IEC 60076-1)

tapping.direction: a higher position removes HV turns and raises the LV voltage
tapping.source: Tapping range +/-10 % in 16 steps of 1.25 % on the HV winding: assumption: typical value, replace with your nameplate. Within the VACUTAP VRS III 700 Y limits published by MR (max. 4500 V step voltage, max. 35 positions with change-over selector, 700 A).

oltc.source: MR VACUTAP VR flyer: 700 A, 4500 V, 300,000 tap-change operations without maintenance; interrupter replacement after 600,000 operations (the figure MR gives for arc-furnace duty, used here as the interrupter life at rated current). Time-based inspection after 10 years, wear per operation proportional to (switched current / rated current)^2 and 30 operations per day: assumption: typical value, replace with the operating instructions of your tap-changer and your regulation history.

regulator.source: MR TAPCON operating instructions: the bandwidth must always be greater than 0.6 x step voltage / nominal voltage x 100 %; delay time T1 20 s at commissioning. Setpoint and the +/-1.0 % band: assumption: typical value, replace with your regulator settings.

motor.source: Duration of one tap change (Megger: usually 3 to 10 s for resistor-type OLTCs) and mean motor current during the change, with +0.6 % per K below 20 degC for thicker grease: assumption: typical value, replace with the commissioning signature of your motor-drive unit.

thermal.source: Normal OLTC compartment oil temperature minus main-tank top-oil temperature: assumption: typical value, replace with your commissioning trend. A healthy compartment runs cooler than the main tank (T&D World, differential temperature monitoring).

dga.source: Background gases of the main tank: assumption: typical value, replace with your DGA history. A vacuum OLTC compartment normally shows gases in the same range as the main tank (Transformer Magazine tap-changer column); IEEE C57.139 gives the LTC interpretation (not read: the excess limits are assumptions).

bushings.source: Nameplate C1 and tan delta at 20 degC of the three HV bushings: assumption: typical value, replace with the rating plates or routine test reports. Order of magnitude: a short between two layers raises C1 by about 4 % in a 138 kV bushing with 20 to 30 layers; healthy OIP power factor around 0.25 % (Transformer Technology).

demo.note: Demo only: the 132 kV grid voltage swings +/-3 % over 6 minutes so the regulator changes taps every minute or so. The counters (operations per day and per year, wear, years since maintenance) and the gas levels come from the failure modes, not from the demo clock.

groups.DGA: Dissolved gases, OLTC and main tank

points.label: Mean motor current, last tap change
Duration of the last tap change
Operations since the last OLTC maintenance
Years since the last OLTC maintenance
Sum of (switched current / rated current)^2 since new interrupters

limits.source: C1 limits 5 % / 10 %: MR MSENSE BM recommendation. tan delta: alert at twice the nameplate value (commonly applied) and at 0.7 % (the IEC 60137 limit for new OIP bushings as commonly quoted, used here as a service alarm). All other limits: assumption: typical value, replace with your own alarm philosophy.

failure_modes.$comment: Each failure mode: what degrades, how it shows, the rules that see it.

contact_wear.name: Vacuum interrupter contacts near end of life
contact_wear.symptoms: accumulated (I/Ir)^2 of the switched current approaches the interrupter life

vacuum_loss.name: Vacuum interrupter loss of vacuum (arc in oil)
vacuum_loss.symptoms: acetylene in the OLTC oil far above the main tank

drive_stiff.name: Motor drive or mechanism stiff
drive_stiff.symptoms: motor current and tap-change duration up at the same cabinet temperature

tap_sensor_fault.name: Tap-position transmitter fault
tap_sensor_fault.symptoms: reported tap disagrees with the LV voltage the windings must give

band_too_narrow.name: Hunting: regulator bandwidth set too narrow
band_too_narrow.symptoms: bandwidth below 0.6 step, operations per day several times normal

compartment_heating.name: Diverter compartment overheating (poor contact)
compartment_heating.symptoms: OLTC oil warmer than the main tank, ethylene in the OLTC oil

bushing_layer_short.name: HV bushing partial breakdown (layer short, C1 step up)
bushing_layer_short.symptoms: C1 of one bushing up by several %, tan delta unchanged

bushing_moisture.name: HV bushing moisture or ageing (tan delta up)
bushing_moisture.symptoms: tan delta of one bushing up, C1 unchanged
